title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Recording a Customer Remittance
content:
## Clause

The former opening provision, which simply had a remittance applied to one acceptance, is **no longer in force**; the current basis on which a remittance may be applied to a Dangerous Goods Acceptance file replaces it.

The provisions that follow remain in force. A remittance is written with the remittance reference exactly as the customer quoted it and with the amount remitted. What is applied may not go beyond the charges the acceptance owes; any excess is returned by finance and never booked. A given remittance reference is recorded no more than once on one acceptance.

## Amount applied

The amount entered is the smaller of the sum remitted and the charges the acceptance owes at the time.

**Illustration with invented amounts.**

| Remitted | Charges owed | Amount entered | Excess handled by finance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 300.00 | 500.00 | 300.00 | none |
| 500.00 | 500.00 | 500.00 | none |
| 650.00 | 500.00 | 500.00 | 150.00 returned, not booked |

## Points of judgement

**The customer quotes a reference with spaces and a hyphen. How is it written?** Character for character as quoted.

**The same reference is quoted again for the same acceptance.** It is not recorded a second time on that acceptance.

superseded_clauses: A remittance is applied to one acceptance,
